subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should the managed daemon heap mitigation land as a fixed generated default now, or should maintainers require a first-class heap tuning surface before resolving this issue?
rationale: The issue affects core Gateway availability, but the available fixes change managed service startup defaults and interact with an intentional NODE_OPTIONS security boundary, so the default-size and operator-tuning tradeoff needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Land the fixed default
options.body: Accept the open PR's fixed 8192 MB generated service default as the emergency mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

options.title: Require tuning first
options.body: Pause the fix until a CLI/config/doctor-owned heap tuning surface is designed and proven for upgrades.

options.title: Choose a CLI-argv shape
options.body: Revive the CLI-argument approach only if maintainers prefer avoiding NODE_OPTIONS entirely and are willing to repair downstream argv assumptions.

recommendation.title: Land the fixed default
recommendation.body: Accept the open PR's fixed 8192 MB generated service default as the emergency mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The daemon install/default tradeoff is in the historical daemon service area where this handle has authored and been routed for related work.
